description: During dream-cycle step-03b, called systems/eval-harness/record-step.py against today's newly-created eval record (eval-20260911T080732-2RJ1NJ.json) before setting its `name` field to "dream-cycle". record-step.py selects its target by matching `name == workflow_name` across all records and picking the most recent by `started`, so with today's record still named "unknown" the three record-step calls silently matched and overwrote the `steps` array on yesterday's closed, successful eval record (eval-20260910T080853-46O0ZP.json) instead, replacing its historical 2026-09-10 step timestamps with today's.
correction: Caught immediately on post-write verification (diffed the target record's steps against expectation, noticed the wrong file had changed). Restored the historical record via `git checkout HEAD -- systems/eval-harness/runs/eval-20260910T080853-46O0ZP.json`, then set `name`/`agent`/`session_id`/`tags` on today's record before re-issuing the three record-step.py calls, which then correctly targeted today's record.
systemic_fix: record-step.py's name-based lookup silently targets the wrong record when a fresh new-eval.py record hasn't had its name field set yet, with no safeguard against overwriting a closed/success record. Proposed: (1) new-eval.py should accept a --name argument so callers set it at creation time rather than as a separate follow-up step; (2) record-step.py should refuse (or at least warn) when the matched target record has status:success/complete, since a step should never be recorded against an already-closed run. Flagging for Rigby.
